newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks post biggest gain since March.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks post biggest gain since March.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks staged a powerful advance on Monday, with the Hang Seng index registering its biggest point gain since March, as new records on Wall Street and strong interest in China shares kept buyers active.
The Hang Seng rose 227.56 points to 12,133.07. Turnover was a heavy HK$8.56 billion versus Friday's HK$6.87 billion.
"It's heavy because investors are confident," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
"Investors are really encouraged by what we saw in the States and the possibility that interest rates will not have to be raised so quickly," said Rossiter.
A surprisingly weak U.S. September jobs report on Friday quelled fears of higher interest rates, pushing the Dow industrials to a record close of 5,992.86, up 60.01 points.
Monday's Hang Seng close was the highest since February 4, 1994 when the blue chip index closed at 12,157.57.
Monday's gain was the biggest since March 19 when the index rose 279.22 points. The Hang Seng index now lies just 68 points short of its record close of 12,201.09 hit on January 4, 1994.
The Hang Seng hit an intra-day high of 12,153.46 on Monday.
"This is one of the biggest days we have had for a long time. No one is selling," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
"We are in an environment where the jury has been out on U.S. rates and they look like they are going to stay steady in the short to medium term. That is what people are betting on."
While some analysts said the market was looking overheated, they said there was still plenty of appetite for stocks.

"Rallies generally have a tendency to overshoot themselves. We could hit 12,200 to 12,300 before we come into a correction but right now everyone is painting a rosy picture of Hong Kong," said Rossiter. He pointed to optimism about corporate earnings, foreign interest in the local market and increased weightings for the Hong Kong market.
HSBC was a strong mover, rising to an all-time high of HK$147.50 during the session before closing at HK$146.40, up HK$3.00. Hang Seng Bank closed at a record HK$86.00, up HK$2.25.
The H-share index of China incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong rose 21.69 points to 855.58.
Among the China-related issues, Glorious Sun jumped HK$0.75 to HK$4.60, CITIC Pacific added HK$1.10 to HK$36.00 and Shanghai Industrial rose HK$1.00 to HK$19.45.
